body.title: [v17.0/forgejo] fix: avoid loading unnecessary data during tag creation
body.body:
**Backport:** https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14785

I noticed that creating a tag via the web UI of codeberg.org was quite
slow (28-30s).

Tracing showed a interesting SQL query:

```sql
SELECT * FROM `attachment` WHERE `release_id` IN (0) ORDER BY `release_id` ASC, `name` ASC
```

Just before tracing showed that Forgejo was doing a lot of
application (non git/DB) code.

---

- `release_service.CreateNewTag` is called from the web router to handle
creating a new tag, this function prepares a release struct with all the
necessary information (every tag is stored as a release in the
database).
- `createTag` is then called which as first thing calls
`LoadAttributes`.
- `LoadAttributes` assumes the given release was loaded from the
database and thus assumes the ID is non-zero. Loading 148026 attachments
into this release.

body.title: testing: Exercise config file path test in temporary directory
body.body:
The `CustomConf` test case ran in whatever the current working directory was (likely the source tree), leaving behind an ini file if the configuration happened to be modified by the exercised code.

We now change the working directory to a temporary directory momentarily. Note that `t.Chdir()` uses the equivalent of `defer` (`Cleanup`).

Noticed with a change which adds ini modifications, see https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14778#issuecomment-24963225
